union.summary: New required `Store.getUsedBounds()` — other Store implementations outside the diff are not updated
union.evidence: `Store` gains a non-optional `getUsedBounds(): Promise<Range | undefined>` (packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts, new member). Only three implementations are updated: MemStore, ReadOnlyStore, YorkieStore. The diff itself points at another: packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts `buildDependantsMap` doc comment says "Unlike the `IDBStore` implementation, this builds the map from the entire grid" — an `IDBStore` exists and is not in the changed-files list, so it (and any test fake/mock implementing `Store`, e.g. in packages/sheets/test/** or packages/frontend) no longer satisfies the interface and fails to compile. Fix belongs on the missing implementations, or make the member optional with a default. NOTE: I could not run Grep — the working tree was not present at the sandbox CWD (/tmp/eval-item-hRoO8Z/repo contains only diff.patch, changed-files.txt, issue-spec.md), so all cross-file claims here are inferred from references visible in the diff and need verification.

union.summary: Blank-skipping in `Arguments.iterate` silently changes semantics for every existing range consumer, not just SUM/AVERAGE
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts `iterate` now does `if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; }`. `iterate` is the shared argument walker for the whole function library (packages/sheets/src/formula/function*.ts — not in the changed-files list), so this changes behaviour for *bounded* ranges too, in functions the diff never considered: `COUNTBLANK(A1:A10)` can now only ever see non-blank cells (→ 0), `COUNTA`/`ROWS`/`COLUMNS`-style cardinality changes, and `AVERAGE(A1:A3)` with a blank A2 now divides by 2 instead of 3 — a behaviour change for existing user formulas that have nothing to do with unbounded ranges. Verify each consumer of `Arguments.iterate`/`ref` in packages/sheets/src/formula/.

union.summary: Dropping blank cells breaks positional/array consumers (INDEX, MATCH, VLOOKUP, TRANSPOSE, spill shape)
union.evidence: The same `continue` in packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts changes the *cardinality and position* of the cells yielded for a range, not just their values. Any consumer that relies on the yielded sequence lining up with the range's geometry — `INDEX`/`MATCH`/`VLOOKUP` offsets, `TRANSPOSE`/`SORT`/`FILTER`, and `evaluateWithSpill`'s `{ values, rows, cols }` shape used in packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts — will now see fewer values than `rows*cols` when the range contains blanks, producing shifted results or a shape mismatch when the spill is written back. The bypassing sites are the array/lookup functions in packages/sheets/src/formula/ (not in the diff); they need to keep receiving blanks (e.g. gate the skip on an aggregation flag) rather than being silently re-shaped.

union.summary: `extractFormulaRanges` (highlighting) now receives REFERENCE tokens it cannot parse — the claimed "skips unbounded refs" behaviour is only in the docs
union.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (new 'Limitations' paragraph) states "Whole-column/row highlighting (`extractFormulaRanges`) skips unbounded refs", but no change to `extractFormulaRanges` appears anywhere in the diff. Its implementation (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts, documented as 'Each REFERENCE token is parsed into a Range') calls `parseRange`/`parseRef`, and `parseRef('A')` throws `Invalid Reference` (see the new `parsePartialRef` in packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts, which exists precisely because `parseRef` cannot handle a column-only endpoint). Now that `A:A`/`1:1` lex as REFERENCE, typing `=SUM(A:A)` into the formula bar routes an unparsable token into the highlighter and can throw on every keystroke. Fix belongs in `extractFormulaRanges` (guard with `isUnboundedRange`) or its frontend caller.

union.summary: `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` (row/column insert-delete, copy/paste) were never taught about unbounded REFERENCE tokens
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/index.ts exports `shiftSref`, `shiftFormula`, `shiftDimensionMap` (visible in the export list touched by this diff). These rewrite REFERENCE tokens of stored formulas when rows/columns are inserted or deleted and when formulas are copied. They are not in the changed-files list, yet the token shape they consume just widened to include `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B`. If they call `parseRef`/`parseRange` on each endpoint, an insert-row on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` either throws mid-mutation or writes back a corrupted formula — persisted data loss. The site needing the fix is `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` in packages/sheets/src/formula/ (pass through unbounded refs unchanged).

union.summary: Expansion clamps to used bounds that include the formula cell itself, creating self-references / cycles the dependency engine assumes cannot exist
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts expands `cell.f` against `await sheet.getUsedBounds()`, and `CellIndex.bounds()` (packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts) covers *all* populated cells including the formula cells themselves. A formula placed inside the band it references — e.g. `=SUM(1:1)` in D1, or `=SUM(A:A)` in A5 — expands to a range that contains its own cell, so `buildDependantsMap` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts) records the cell as its own dependant. That violates the acyclicity invariant the topological recalculation/cycle detection relies on; expect a spurious `#REF!`/cycle error or a recalculation loop. Note the new tests deliberately place every formula in column D outside rows 1-3 (packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts, the `=SUM(1:3)` case at r5,c4), so this case is never exercised.

union.summary: Dependants map and grid fetch now enumerate every cell of an expanded range on every edit
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts now wrap each formula in `expandUnboundedRanges(...)` before `toSrefs(extractReferences(...))`, and the calculator does `sheet.fetchGridByReferences(references)` on the expanded formula. `toSrefs` materialises one `Sref` per cell in the range, so a single `=SUM(A:A)` on a sheet whose used bounds are thousands of rows adds thousands of dependants-map keys, rebuilt on *every* edit (the docs note "the dependants map is rebuilt on every edit"). Callers of `toSrefs`/`fetchGridByReferences` outside the diff were written for small hand-written ranges. Worth confirming against the largest realistic sheet before shipping.

union.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs are left unexpanded and flow into cross-sheet resolution paths that cannot parse them
union.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges` in packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts deliberately skips `isCrossSheetRef(token.text)`, but the grammar change (packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4, `REFERENCE: QUOTED_SHEET_NAME '!' REFRANGE | SHEET_NAME '!' REFRANGE`) makes `Sheet2!A:A` lex successfully for the first time. That token now reaches `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` and the cross-sheet resolution helpers (`parseCrossSheetRef`, `getWorksheetCell` — imported in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts), none of which are in this diff. The docs claim it "evaluate[s] to `#ERROR!`"; verify it does not instead throw out of `parseRange` and abort the whole recalculation pass.

union.summary: `isUnboundedRange` and `resolveRange` are exported from coordinates.ts but not re-exported from the package entry point
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/index.ts adds only `expandUnboundedRanges` to the export list, alongside existing coordinate helpers such as `isCrossSheetRef`/`parseCrossSheetRef`. The two new public helpers in packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts (`isUnboundedRange`, `resolveRange`) are unreachable from packages/frontend, which is the package that has to decide how to render/select an unbounded range (yorkie-store.ts already imports coordinate helpers through the entry point). Any frontend code needing to detect an unbounded ref has no supported way to do so.

union.summary: Formula-editor helpers around REFERENCE tokens may assume a full `col+row` reference
union.evidence: packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts imports `isReferenceInsertPosition`, `findReferenceTokenAtCursor`, `normalizeFormulaOnCommit` from packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts — the reference-picking / click-to-insert path used by the formula bar. None were changed, yet the REFERENCE token shape they inspect now includes `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B`. If any of them uppercase-and-`parseRef` the matched token (as `normalizeFormulaOnCommit` plausibly does), editing a formula containing a whole-column ref throws or silently rewrites it. Needs a read of those three functions to confirm.

union.summary: Regenerated lexer inserts COL/ROW into the rule list — any consumer keyed on numeric token/rule indices shifts
union.evidence: packages/sheets/antlr/FormulaLexer.ts `ruleNames` now inserts "COL", "ROW" before "REF", and packages/sheets/antlr/FormulaLexer.interp adds COL/ROW to the token-name block, shifting every subsequent rule index (the serialized ATN action index moves from `\b\x11` to `\b\x13`). Code that maps token *type numbers* rather than symbolic names — e.g. a syntax-highlighting colour table in packages/frontend keyed on raw `token.type` — would silently mis-classify. `extractTokens` uses the vocabulary so it is fine; the risk is any frontend consumer of raw token types.

union.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs (`Sheet2!A:A`) are deliberately left unexpanded, but now lex as REFERENCE tokens and reach `toSrefs`, which throws `Invalid Reference` — breaking `buildDependantsMap` for the ENTIRE sheet, not just that cell. The `isCrossSheetRef(r) continue` guard in the loop body cannot help: the generator throws while producing the value, before any iteration happens.
union.evidence: memory.ts:333 `for (const r of toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds))))` — expandUnboundedRanges skips cross-sheet (formula.ts:364), so `SHEET2!A:A` survives; toSrefs (coordinates.ts:236-243) takes the cross-sheet branch, `localRef='A:A'` contains ':', so `parseRange('A:A')` → `parseRef('A')` → throw (coordinates.ts:336-338). Same three sites in the diff's other store: yorkie-store.ts:574, :586, :602. Callers do not catch: sheet.ts:1063 (`setData`) and :1144 (`removeData`) only have `finally { endBatch() }`, so one cell containing `=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)` makes every later edit in the sheet throw.

union.summary: `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` calls `toSrefs` on the calculator's unexpanded cross-sheet unbounded reference and throws, aborting the whole recalculation pass instead of yielding `#ERROR!` as the design doc promises.
union.evidence: calculator.ts:94-95 passes `extractReferences(formula)` (still containing `SHEET2!A:A`) into `sheet.fetchGridByReferences`, whose first statement is `for (const sref of toSrefs(references))` at sheet.ts:2615 → parseRange('A:A') throws. Unlike `evaluate`/`evaluateWithSpill` (formula.ts:547,569 wrap in try/catch → ErrValue.ERROR), this throw is outside any catch, so it escapes `calculate()` and kills recalculation for every remaining cell in `sorted`. Contradicts docs/design/sheets/formula.md:128-131 ("evaluate to `#ERROR!`"). Fix belongs either here or in the new calculator code (expand or drop cross-sheet unbounded refs).

union.summary: `Sheet.buildGlobalDependantsMap` extracts references straight from raw `cell.f` with no `expandUnboundedRanges` call, so a purely LOCAL `=SUM(A:A)` throws there and breaks cross-sheet recalculation.
union.evidence: sheet.ts:2711-2712 `const references = extractReferences(cell.f); for (const ref of toSrefs(references))` and again at sheet.ts:2736-2738 for every formula of every remote sheet. Neither was updated to expand, so `A:A` → parseRange → parseRef('A') → throw. Reached from `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2773-2804) whenever the sheet holds any cross-sheet formula, e.g. a cell `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!B1`.

union.summary: `shiftFormula` splits a range token and calls `parseARef` on each endpoint, which throws for `A` or `1` — so inserting or deleting a row/column on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` now throws mid-operation instead of shifting the formula.
union.evidence: shifting.ts:372-374 `const [startStr, endStr] = text.split(':'); parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase())` — parseARef requires `/^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$/` and throws otherwise (coordinates.ts:366-369). Reached from shiftGrid (shifting.ts:456) ← MemStore.shiftCells (memory.ts:181) and from yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:289. The store has already begun mutating (grid replaced/doc updated) when the throw happens, so the structural edit can land half-applied.

union.summary: `relocateFormula` has the same unguarded `parseARef` on range endpoints, so copy/paste and autofill of any formula containing a whole-column/row range now throws.
union.evidence: shifting.ts:183-185 `const [startStr, endStr] = text.split(':'); relocateARef(parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase()), ...)`. Callers: clipboard.ts:25 (`relocateFormula(cell.f, deltaRow, deltaCol)` while building the pasted grid) and clipboard.ts:151. Pasting `=SUM(A:A)` — a formula the new grammar now accepts and users will type — throws instead of pasting.

union.summary: `moveFormula` and `redirectFormula` also parse range endpoints with `parseARef`, so moving rows/columns and cut-paste reference redirection throw on unbounded refs.
union.evidence: shifting.ts:79-81 (`moveFormula`, reached from moveGrid shifting.ts:120 ← MemStore.moveCells memory.ts:233 and yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:359) and shifting.ts:241-243 (`redirectFormula`, reached from sheet.ts:2375 `redirectFormulasForCut`, itself called at sheet.ts:2191 and :2321). Both call `parseARef` on `A` / `1`, which throws (coordinates.ts:366-369).

union.summary: The new blank-cell skip in `Arguments.iterate` is applied to every range, not just unbounded ones, silently changing results of existing bounded-range formulas for all consumers of the shared iterator.
union.evidence: arguments.ts:116-123 skips any blank cell whenever `isSrng(node.v)`. Unconsidered consumers: functions-logical.ts:111 (`AND`), :133 (`OR`), :174 (`XOR`) — a blank in `=AND(A1:A3)` used to yield `false` via ref2bool (arguments.ts:194) and short-circuit FALSE; it is now skipped, so the result flips to TRUE. functions-math.ts:247 (`PRODUCT`) used to return 0 for a range containing a blank, now returns the product of non-blanks; also :874 (`GCD`), :898 (`LCM`), :1392 (`SUMSQ`). functions-statistical.ts:31 (`AVERAGE` divisor), :56 (`MEDIAN`), :645/:670 (`STDEV`), :695/:720 (`VAR`), :745 (`MODE`), :1242/:1261/:1280/:1299 all change their value sets. Only MIN/MAX have tests for the new semantics (test/formula/formula.test.ts:4412-4437); the boolean and product consumers have none.

union.summary: `YorkieStore.getUsedBounds()` reads a cell index rebuilt from document keys only, while every other read merges `batchOverlay`, so bounds can be stale inside a batch and clamp `A:A` to the wrong extent in the collaborative store.
union.evidence: ensureIndex (yorkie-store.ts:194-204) rebuilds from `this.worksheetKeys(ws)` — document cells only — whereas getGrid explicitly consults the overlay (yorkie-store.ts:451-456) and set() only patches the index incrementally when `!this.dirty` (yorkie-store.ts:266-273). So after any dirty-invalidation during an open batch (paste/multi-cell edit), `bounds()` at :567 and :616 omits overlay-written cells and still counts overlay-deleted ones, and the calculator (calculator.ts:90-93) expands `A:A` against that stale extent.

union.summary: `calculate()` now awaits `getUsedBounds()` once per formula cell, and the store implementations recompute it by scanning the whole index each time — a new O(formula cells × populated cells) cost on every recalculation.
union.evidence: calculator.ts:90-93 calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` inside the `for (const sref of sorted)` loop; sheet.ts:2604-2606 delegates to the store; yorkie-store.ts:615-617 runs `ensureIndex()` plus `cellIndex.bounds()`, which iterates every key of rowIndex and colIndex (cell-index.ts:128-152). The value cannot change during the loop, so hoisting it out would remove the regression.

union.summary: Formula-editor token highlighting now colours bare `A:A`/`1:1` as references, but the range-highlight path can skip them, leaving the two consumers inconsistent.
union.evidence: cellinput.ts:336-341 and formulabar.ts:191-194 colour every REFERENCE token by index (`refIndex++`), while extractFormulaRanges (formula.ts:414-417) returns nothing for an unbounded ref when no bounds are supplied — so the reference-colour index and the highlighted-range list can fall out of sync for formulas mixing `A:A` with ordinary refs.

per_sample.evidence: sheet.ts:2711-2712 `const references = extractReferences(cell.f); for (const ref of toSrefs(references))` and again at sheet.ts:2736-2738 for every formula of every remote sheet. Neither was updated to expand, so `A:A` → parseRange → parseRef('A') → throw. Reached from `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2773-2804) whenever the sheet holds any cross-sheet formula, e.g. a cell `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!B1`.

per_sample.summary: `shiftFormula` splits a range token and calls `parseARef` on each endpoint, which throws for `A` or `1` — so inserting or deleting a row/column on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` now throws mid-operation instead of shifting the formula.
per_sample.evidence: shifting.ts:372-374 `const [startStr, endStr] = text.split(':'); parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase())` — parseARef requires `/^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$/` and throws otherwise (coordinates.ts:366-369). Reached from shiftGrid (shifting.ts:456) ← MemStore.shiftCells (memory.ts:181) and from yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:289. The store has already begun mutating (grid replaced/doc updated) when the throw happens, so the structural edit can land half-applied.

per_sample.summary: `relocateFormula` has the same unguarded `parseARef` on range endpoints, so copy/paste and autofill of any formula containing a whole-column/row range now throws.
per_sample.evidence: shifting.ts:183-185 `const [startStr, endStr] = text.split(':'); relocateARef(parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase()), ...)`. Callers: clipboard.ts:25 (`relocateFormula(cell.f, deltaRow, deltaCol)` while building the pasted grid) and clipboard.ts:151. Pasting `=SUM(A:A)` — a formula the new grammar now accepts and users will type — throws instead of pasting.

per_sample.summary: `moveFormula` and `redirectFormula` also parse range endpoints with `parseARef`, so moving rows/columns and cut-paste reference redirection throw on unbounded refs.
per_sample.evidence: shifting.ts:79-81 (`moveFormula`, reached from moveGrid shifting.ts:120 ← MemStore.moveCells memory.ts:233 and yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:359) and shifting.ts:241-243 (`redirectFormula`, reached from sheet.ts:2375 `redirectFormulasForCut`, itself called at sheet.ts:2191 and :2321). Both call `parseARef` on `A` / `1`, which throws (coordinates.ts:366-369).

per_sample.summary: The new blank-cell skip in `Arguments.iterate` is applied to every range, not just unbounded ones, silently changing results of existing bounded-range formulas for all consumers of the shared iterator.
per_sample.evidence: arguments.ts:116-123 skips any blank cell whenever `isSrng(node.v)`. Unconsidered consumers: functions-logical.ts:111 (`AND`), :133 (`OR`), :174 (`XOR`) — a blank in `=AND(A1:A3)` used to yield `false` via ref2bool (arguments.ts:194) and short-circuit FALSE; it is now skipped, so the result flips to TRUE. functions-math.ts:247 (`PRODUCT`) used to return 0 for a range containing a blank, now returns the product of non-blanks; also :874 (`GCD`), :898 (`LCM`), :1392 (`SUMSQ`). functions-statistical.ts:31 (`AVERAGE` divisor), :56 (`MEDIAN`), :645/:670 (`STDEV`), :695/:720 (`VAR`), :745 (`MODE`), :1242/:1261/:1280/:1299 all change their value sets. Only MIN/MAX have tests for the new semantics (test/formula/formula.test.ts:4412-4437); the boolean and product consumers have none.

per_sample.summary: `YorkieStore.getUsedBounds()` reads a cell index rebuilt from document keys only, while every other read merges `batchOverlay`, so bounds can be stale inside a batch and clamp `A:A` to the wrong extent in the collaborative store.
per_sample.evidence: ensureIndex (yorkie-store.ts:194-204) rebuilds from `this.worksheetKeys(ws)` — document cells only — whereas getGrid explicitly consults the overlay (yorkie-store.ts:451-456) and set() only patches the index incrementally when `!this.dirty` (yorkie-store.ts:266-273). So after any dirty-invalidation during an open batch (paste/multi-cell edit), `bounds()` at :567 and :616 omits overlay-written cells and still counts overlay-deleted ones, and the calculator (calculator.ts:90-93) expands `A:A` against that stale extent.

per_sample.summary: `calculate()` now awaits `getUsedBounds()` once per formula cell, and the store implementations recompute it by scanning the whole index each time — a new O(formula cells × populated cells) cost on every recalculation.
per_sample.evidence: calculator.ts:90-93 calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` inside the `for (const sref of sorted)` loop; sheet.ts:2604-2606 delegates to the store; yorkie-store.ts:615-617 runs `ensureIndex()` plus `cellIndex.bounds()`, which iterates every key of rowIndex and colIndex (cell-index.ts:128-152). The value cannot change during the loop, so hoisting it out would remove the regression.

per_sample.summary: Formula-editor token highlighting now colours bare `A:A`/`1:1` as references, but the range-highlight path can skip them, leaving the two consumers inconsistent.
per_sample.evidence: cellinput.ts:336-341 and formulabar.ts:191-194 colour every REFERENCE token by index (`refIndex++`), while extractFormulaRanges (formula.ts:414-417) returns nothing for an unbounded ref when no bounds are supplied — so the reference-colour index and the highlighted-range list can fall out of sync for formulas mixing `A:A` with ordinary refs.
